title: Live election results: Raman increases lead over Bass in LA mayoral race
text:
2026 election results: Live midterm results for California governor's race, LA mayor race, Prop 40, more - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Live POLITICS 
 Live election results: Raman increases lead over Bass in LA mayoral race 
 Stream Southern California's News Leader and Original Shows 24/7 Last updated: Thursday, November 5, 2026 2:12AM GMT Share Follow ABC7 on Google Voters have cast their ballot to decide the next California governor, Los Angeles' next mayor, whether or not to pass 14 statewide propositions and more.
 Polls closed in California, and Democrat Xavier Becerra was quickly projected to win in the governor's race over Republican Steve Hilton.
 Meanwhile, a winner has not been projected in the Los Angeles mayoral race as votes continue to be counted.
 Here are live updates and everything you need to know about the midterm elections.

 Here's how the news is developing. By Bianca Buono 2:13 AM GMT 
 Democrat Derek Tran wins reelection in California's 45th Congressional District 
 Democratic Congressman Derek Tran has won reelection in District 45, beating Republican challenger Chuong Vo by more than 30,000 votes.
 Leading up to Election Day, the race for California's 45th Congressional district was viewed as a competitive one and a race to watch, but Tran was projected as the winner hours after polls closed.
 Democratic Congressman Derek Tran has won reelection in District 45, beating Republican challenger Chuong Vo. Tran, who flipped the district blue back in 2024, is an Army veteran and the son of Vietnamese refugees. Vo, who is also Vietnamese American, previously served as mayor of Cerritos and is a retired police officer.
 Federal data shows Tran raised nearly $6 million while Vo's campaign brought in $937,000. 
 12:36 AM GMT 
 Raman widens lead over Bass in latest LA mayor's race results 
 Los Angeles Councilmember Nithya Raman widened her lead over Mayor Karen Bass in the latest L.A. mayor's race results.
 Raman sits at 405,193 votes, while Bass sits at 379,069, with 67% of the expected vote in.
 The race remains too close to call.

 Los Angeles Councilmember Nithya Raman maintains a lead over Mayor Karen Bass in the latest L.A. mayor's race results. Nov 04, 2026, 11:35 PM GMT 
 Incoming House Oversight chair vows 4 new probes into Trump administration 
 Rep. Robert Garcia, the presumptive chairman of the House Oversight Committee, said the panel would launch several new investigations into the Trump administration. In a two-word statement released late Tuesday after the Democrats were projected to take control of the House, Rep. Robert Garcia, the presumptive chairman of the House Oversight Committee, stated: "Lawyer up."
 On Wednesday, he expanded on that terse statement during a news conference in Huntington Beach, which is part of the district he'll represent in the next Congress.
 "We should be very clear that the American people have spoken loudly and clearly - they want change," Garcia told reporters. "They are tired of the destruction and the corruption of Donald Trump and this administration."
 Garcia pointed to Democrats' electoral victories nationwide as a mandate. He said the Oversight Committee will be focused on "four major areas" -- alleged corruption by President Trump and his family, "abuses" by the Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the handling of the Epstein files, and companies that he said are "ripping off" the American public.
 Nov 04, 2026, 8:01 PM GMT 
 Voters approve Prop 3, permanently extending a high-income tax 
 Californians have voted to approve Proposition 3, which provides permanent funding for schools and healthcare by extending a tax on high incomes.
 With 99% of votes counted as of Wednesday morning, the measure has received 4,483,291 "yes" votes, or 59%.
 Forty-one percent were against the proposal, with a total of 3,159,553 "no" votes.
 The proposition "maintains $5 billion to $15 billion of annual state income tax revenue by making a temporary tax increase on high-income earners permanent instead of letting it expire in 2031," according to the state's official voter information guide.
 Supporters included the California Teachers Association, CA School Nurses Organization, California State PTA, and Planned Parenthood Affiliates of CA.
 The measure was opposed by the California Taxpayers Association, Family Business Association of California and the California Hispanic Chambers of Commerce.
